segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
DuPont reports in two segments since completing the Qnity Electronics Products spinoff on 1 November 2025: Healthcare & Water Technologies (Water + Healthcare business lines) and Diversified Industrials (Industrial Technologies + Building Technologies/Safety & Construction).

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: prior-period comparisons before the spinoff restate the old Electronics & Industrial segment out of continuing operations, so this chart only reflects the post-spin two-segment structure management now guides to.

What to watch:

  • Diversified Industrials is the more cyclical, shorter-cycle book -- watch it against the general industrial order cycle
  • Healthcare & Water is the steadier, higher-margin segment the equity story leans on post-spin

businessLineRevenue.title: Revenue by business line
businessLineRevenue.content:
The four business lines underneath the two segments: Water and Healthcare (both inside Healthcare & Water Technologies), and Industrial Technologies and Building Technologies (both inside Diversified Industrials).

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: Water is the largest single line and the one most exposed to municipal and industrial water-treatment capex cycles; Building Technologies carries the safety/construction exposure that tracks non-residential construction.

What to watch:

  • Which line is driving segment growth or decline in a given quarter
  • Mix shift toward Water/Healthcare (higher margin) versus Industrial/Building

segmentEbitda.title: Adjusted EBITDA by segment
segmentEbitda.content:
Adjusted EBITDA by segment, plus unallocated Corporate costs (always negative -- management, legal, pension and stranded costs not charged to a segment).

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: Healthcare & Water Technologies has consistently carried a higher segment margin than Diversified Industrials; a segment's EBITDA growing slower than its revenue is margin dilution worth tracing to mix or input costs.

What to watch:

  • Corporate costs shrinking as one-off separation costs from the Qnity spin roll off
  • Segment margin spread narrowing or widening over time

organicGrowthBridge.title: Organic growth bridge
organicGrowthBridge.content:
Management's standard bridge from prior-year revenue to the current period: volume (units sold) and price/mix together make up organic growth; currency translation and portfolio (acquisitions/divestitures, including the Qnity carve-out) are the non-organic pieces. The four bars sum to total reported revenue growth.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: the portfolio bar is dominated by the Qnity divestiture around the FY2025/FY2026 boundary -- read it alongside the spinoff date, not as an ongoing M&A cadence.

What to watch:

  • Price/mix turning negative (pricing pressure, not just a softer volume quarter)
  • Currency swinging the total growth rate independent of the operating business

segmentOrganicGrowth.title: Organic growth by segment
segmentOrganicGrowth.content:
The volume + price/mix organic growth rate (currency and portfolio effects excluded) for each segment separately, rather than the blended company-wide rate.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: the two segments have moved in different directions quarter to quarter (Healthcare & Water weaker in FY2024, Diversified Industrials weaker in FY2025) -- the blended OrganicGrowth KPI can mask an offsetting swing in either segment.

What to watch:

  • Both segments decelerating at once versus an offsetting mix shift
  • Which segment is carrying the company-wide organic growth figure in a given period

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For DuPont de Nemours, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
